title: 2018 AMC 12A Problem 16
statement: Which of the following describes the set of values of \(a\) for which the curves \(x^2 + y^2 = a^2\) and \(y = x^2 - a\) in the real \(xy\)-plane intersect at exactly \(3\) points?

solutions.text:
Substituting \(x^2 = y + a\) into \(x^2 + y^2 = a^2\) gives \(y^2 + y + (a - a^2) = 0,\) which factors as \((y + 1 - a)(y + a) = 0,\) so \(y = a - 1\) or \(y = -a.\) These correspond to \(x^2 = 2a - 1\) and \(x^2 = 0.\)

The equation \(x^2 = 0\) always gives the single point \((0, -a),\) the vertex of the parabola. The equation \(x^2 = 2a - 1\) gives two more points exactly when \(2a - 1 \gt 0,\) i.e. \(a \gt \tfrac12.\) So there are \(3\) intersection points precisely when \(a \gt \tfrac12.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: From \(y = x^2 - a\) substitute \(x^2 = y + a\) into the circle equation to get a quadratic in \(y\)
One intersection is the vertex tangency at \(x = 0;\) two more require \(x^2 = 2a - 1\) to have real nonzero solutions
